chunks.content: Wrote a blog post explaining why we chose NOT to adopt Kubernetes for our small-team deployment pipeline.
Operated a single-node Docker Compose stack in production for two years with 99.95% uptime.
Migrated a legacy monolith onto Kubernetes on GKE, wrote the Helm charts, and owned the rollout runbook.
Recreational rock climbing at V4 grade.
Reviewed an unrelated team's Terraform modules for AWS EKS clusters and flagged three IAM privilege-escalation risks.

query: Platform engineer to migrate legacy services to Kubernetes on GKE with Helm chart deployments.
notes: Only chunk 2 reflects real hands-on Kubernetes production work on GKE with Helm. Chunk 0 contains the keyword 'Kubernetes' but the person did NOT do Kubernetes work. Chunk 4 is adjacent (EKS but read-only review). Chunk 1 is anti-signal. Chunk 3 is a distractor. QUERY REDESIGN (v1.2.M2): 'Kubernetes GKE Helm' produces AND-tsquery 'kubernete' & 'gke' & 'helm'. Chunk 0 has 'kubernete' but NOT 'gke' or 'helm', so the AND-conjunction correctly filters the adversarial chunk. Only chunk 2 has all three terms. This demonstrates AND semantics as a natural adversarial filter — a keyword-only hit on 'Kubernetes' is not enough. Keyword-arm expected hit: chunk 2 only.
